You can't make people like things they don't, and not everyone enjoys the same things as everyone else. However, when you're empathetic about someone you care about, it gives you a level of interest in the topic out of understanding the other person's feelings. It might not match, but it comes from a genuine place. For example, my SO hates sports. I'm a total nerd who is heavily vested into technology, science, et cetera, so it came as a surprise that I was as heavily into sports as I am. I want to talk about sports, share clips of plays, or talk about other sports related cool shit, but that was not up their alley. Over time, my SO developed an understanding of my love for sports and my passion for the strategy, and while not enjoying it personally, became more willing to watch short clips, check something out, hear me tell a story, etc. This hockey season, she actually started to watch some games with me unprompted!

The trick to this, however, is recognizing that this isn't a one-way street. Even with her developing empathy and understanding for my position, that doesn't mean I just show ever every cool sports highlight I find or talk about every game. My SO is not a sports person so certain nuances and the importance of some things are just missed. I show the funny, the interesting, the seemingly-absurd. I gossip about the things athletes do that aren't sports-related. I strike out here-and-there, but it happens. Most importantly, I try and show the same kind of understanding and empathy for things my SO enjoys. At the very least, I try whatever it is they're interested in at least once, so I can gain experience and perspective, and we can talk about it later.
